Fantasy Quadrant

Hot/Cold Index × Weekly Performance

Y-axis (both quadrant panels) = a 4-week "hot/cold index" (RSI math run on each player's own weekly fantasy points within the selected season, relative to their own recent baseline, not other players). Trail = one line from 2 weeks ago straight to this week -- no simulated motion, every slider position is a real past week's stat line.
300 players in report · generated 2026-08-29 19:41 UTC · off-season -- defaulting to the most recent completed season (2025)
Pool = top 300 players by the PPR points in each player's own most recent game, as of 2025 week 18 — a player on bye, hurt or inactive is ranked on the last week they actually played, not dropped (108 of the 300 are ranked on an earlier week; their trend cards say last: wk N). ALL plots the top 40 of that pool; picking a position plots every player at that position in the pool.
Position
Season

Hot/Cold Index × Points Scored

X-axis = actual points scored that week (PPR). Bubble size = usage share -- opportunities (carries + targets) as a share of the player's own team's total that week. Axis range and bubble scale follow whichever players are currently shown, so the top-40 view isn't squashed by the full pool's outliers. Only the week's leaders get name labels; hover any bubble for the rest.
COLD (INDEX < 50)
0
HOT (INDEX > 50)
0
Week 1
Showing: Week 1
Points scored is the volume/production read -- who actually put up the most points, regardless of how efficiently.

Hot/Cold Index × Points Per Touch

X-axis = points scored PER TOUCH that week (touches = carries + receptions, not targets). Same bubble sizing (usage share). This is the efficiency read instead of the volume read.
COLD (INDEX < 50)
0
HOT (INDEX > 50)

Week 1
Showing: Week 1
Points per touch strips out volume -- a bell-cow back getting 20 mediocre touches and a change-of-pace back getting 5 explosive ones can land in very different spots here even in a week they scored the same total points.

4-Season Points Trend (2023–2026)

Weekly PPR points, chronological, across as much of the last 4 regular seasons as each player actually has -- a rookie or a recent addition just starts wherever their real data starts. Each point is a bubble sized by that game's points per play (touches), scaled relative to every game, for every player, in this report -- so bubble size never changes when you filter. Hover or click any point to see that exact game's stats below its card. Dashed lines always mark season boundaries, regardless of which seasons are checked below. Cards follow the position filter above, and always cover the same 4-season span independent of the season selected in the panels.
